text: dsh-system1-observer 是面向 DSH Web 的循环观测插件：它在配置的 agent 循环节点旁调用 System One 模型，并把请求、回答和跳过原因记入 JSONL 跟踪文件。默认关注 admit、draft、pre_execute 和 post_execute 等节点；也可读取已结束的会话并生成评估记录。插件提供跟踪查询、设置说明、会话评估和测量结果工具，帮助查看模型在不同节点的判断及其耗时。观察调用不会替代循环本身的决定。使用时需要一个可访问的 System One 服务端点；默认地址为本机端点，若服务需要认证，可在环境变量中配置 API key。

dsh-system1-observer calls a System One model at configured DSH loop checkpoints and records answers and skips in a JSONL trace. It can evaluate stored sessions and offers trace and measurement tools. Configure a reachable endpoint; authentication can use an environment variable.
我想查看 DSH 在各个 agent 循环节点调用评估模型时问了什么、得到了什么回答。
能不能把已经结束的 DSH 会话交给模型评估，并保存一份可查看的测量记录？
How can I inspect what an evaluator answered at each configured point in my DSH agent loop?
dsh-system1-observer 的功能「循环节点观测」：在选定的 agent 循环节点调用 System One 模型，并将调用和回答记录到跟踪中。节点通过配置选择；可查询记录中的回答、耗时以及跳过原因。
dsh-system1-observer 的功能「已存会话评估」：可在会话结束后读取整段会话或指定片段，通过配置的问题集请求模型作答，并生成聚合结果。用户通过会话评估工具传入会话标识和片段参数。
dsh-system1-observer 使用前须知：评估文本会发送到配置的 System One 端点；认证密钥可从环境变量读取。（见 core/model/wire.js:26-54；dsh/index.js:182-186）

dsh-system1-observer README · dsh-system1-observer：**Human's words:** This is vibe-coded. Agents could take initiative to, and are mostly free to gather rubric and evaluate using system1 call on parts or whole of sessions.
Almost all is volatile. Agent can change configurations which will be hot-loaded.
Measurement being important, the actions to make use of the evaluation are interesting and useful. 
The "seams" are there to feedback to the human or agent, and the current state of this project provides a flexible basis.

dsh-system1-observer README · dsh-system1-observer：Following is written by agents, self-evaluated and compared notes, with README writing standards they researched and formulated.
These words are results of two LLM in DeepSeek Harness and a TypeSafe jev model in dsh-system1-observer plugin.

--------

**A seam observer for the DeepSeek Harness.** It asks a System One model what the agent loop is doing — at the points
you choose — and writes every call, every skip and every answer to a JSONL trace.

dsh-system1-observer README · dsh-system1-observer：**It decides nothing.** Each listener returns the loop's own decision *by reference*; every trace line says
`enforcement: "declarative", verified: false`. Its product is evidence about the decision model's replies at each point
of the loop, not judgements about the session it is observing.

dsh-system1-observer README · dsh-system1-observer：**This page is short on purpose**: it is capped at 100 lines by `test/readme.test.js`, and the reference material —
every setting, the seams, the trace, and the measured claims **with the ones that are not verified** — is in the
[manual](https://github.com/johnlam1968/dsh-system1-observer/blob/master/docs/manual.md).

dsh-system1-observer README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-system1-observer
```

`web` is the profile to install into — substitute the name of yours. Or from a clone, which needs no npm account:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/johnlam1968/dsh-system1-observer.git
cd dsh-system1-observer && ./install.sh web
```

dsh-system1-observer README · Install：It needs the profile's harness for `@deepseek-ai/cordis` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` (they are **peerDependencies**,
not bundled), and a model to call: the profile's `system1` service, or the HTTP wire at `wireUrl` (default
`http://127.0.0.1:8766`).

dsh-system1-observer README · Sixty seconds：```
system1_explain                                    what it can do, what it is set to now, what a reading covers
session_index_search { query: 'XYZ' }                    find the session  (dsh-session-index)
system1_evaluate_session { sessionId: '…', segmentChars: 57600, package: true }   judge it, and package the run
system1_measurements { action: 'interpret', package: '…', text: '…', by: 'you' }  attach your reading

dsh-system1-observer README · Sixty seconds：`system1_evaluate_session` does the mechanical work in one call: it reads the session, segments it if it is large, asks
every question of every segment, aggregates in code and writes a report package. The last step is a separate call, and
deliberately yours — prose cannot be derived from numbers.

dsh-system1-observer README · Sixty seconds：Nine tools in all: `system1_explain`, `system1_settings`, `system1_decide`, `system1_evaluate_session`,
`system1_measurements`, `system1_session_subject`, `system1_question_sets`, `system1_battery`, `system1_trace`. Finding a session is `dsh-session-index`'s — `session_index_list`/`search`/`refresh`, in milliseconds.

dsh-system1-observer README · What you get：- **The trace**: `~/.dsh/logs/system1-observer.jsonl` — one line per call, per skip and per start-up, read by the
  `system1_trace` tool, the trace card, or `scripts/trace.mjs`.
- **The settings card** on the Plugins page: every live-writable setting, and "…" → **Observe this session**.
- **A written record**: the [register](https://github.com/johnlam1968/dsh-system1-observer/blob/master/docs/findings.md)
  notes every problem this instrument has had and the measurement that found it.

dsh-system1-observer README · Before you trust a reading：1. **Long conversations are summarised** unless you pass `segmentChars` — a large session needs segments.
2. **Where it has no question of its own, it records that it did not ask** rather than guessing.
3. **Its built-in question is measurably weaker at the tool-call points**, so a tool-heavy run reads differently.
4. **Readings either side of a configuration change are not comparable** — every change is written to the trace first.
dsh-system1-observer README · Before you trust a reading：`system1_explain` prints these in full, derived from the running row.
